_summary.jbook_fired_on_note: pentagon_jbook returned NOT_FOUND for all 8 J-Book-grounded claims because the corpus (410 PEs) is heavily weighted to DARPA/MDA/SOCOM/Air Force/Space Force RDT&E and does not cover Navy SCN procurement (Virginia/Columbia/DDG-51), Army OPA (Abrams/Stryker), or DoD-wide IT services IDIQs (SITE III/DEOS/CHS-5) that GD depends on. Heuristic 7 applies: NOT_FOUND ≠ red flag here, it is corpus coverage gap. Usaspending orthogonal cross-check confirmed >$199B in DoD obligations across GD's federal-contracting subs through the cutoff window, validating the claimed revenue base. To make pentagon_jbook discriminative for GD-class primes, the corpus needs Navy SCN line items + Army Combat Vehicle procurement (PE 0603619A, 0203735A, etc.).
_summary.framework_observation: GD is a poor stress-test for the J-Book divergence pattern at this corpus version. The cohort framework presumes companies whose narrative pivots on named RDT&E PEs the J-Book covers; GD's narrative pivots on multi-decade Navy/Army procurement programs structurally outside the v1 corpus. A genuine divergence pattern would require corpus extension or a small-cap with named RDT&E exposure.
